decision_history.rationale: CR-001 and CR-002 resolved, but a narrow two-lens confirmation pass on the CR-001 fix-up diff surfaced and confirmed a new issue, CR-003 (presence-only env-key check could drop a genuinely foreign value under --force).

decision_history.round: human decision (sdlc-light rule: no 3rd automated round)
decision_history.rationale: CR-003 was fixed (value-aware check instead of presence-only) and verified: TDD red->green, regression test added, tsc clean, full project suite green (unit 353 files/5258 tests, integration 37 files/278 tests). The user then explicitly approved proceeding to QA gates rather than requesting a 3rd automated review round, which is this flow's designated human checkpoint after a check-round request-changes. QA gates (Stage 6) subsequently passed in full, and ~25 manual end-to-end scenarios were verified against a real local build in an isolated $HOME, including an exact replay of the ticket's original 9-step repro and both CR-001/CR-003's specific edge cases.

rationale: All three findings from the final and first check round are now resolved. CR-001: alreadyManaged also considers CODEMIE_ENV_KEYS presence, with a regression test (verified GREEN) proving the live bearer token is stripped out of a rebuilt backup for an env-only-managed file. CR-002: resolved via explicit human decision — the user confirmed it is intentional (mirrors the already-accepted codex-desktop precedent; AC3's no-restore redesign makes it functionally safe), so no code change was made or required. CR-003: the presence-only env-key check (`key in existingEnv`) was replaced with a value-aware check (`existingEnv[key] === codemieEnv[key]`), so a genuinely foreign value under a managed key name is preserved via the raw-copy backup path instead of being silently dropped under --force; a regression test proves it, and this was independently re-verified manually (--force + foreign value under a managed key name -> preserved in backup). A stray TypeError concern from the blind lens on `key in existingEnv` was checked directly against the source (`existingEnv = existing.env ?? {}`, line 281) and ruled out as a false positive — existingEnv is always an object. This verdict object was updated after the fact to reflect the CR-003 fix-up and the human's approval decision, since sdlc-light does not run a 3rd automated review round and the prior committed verdict file otherwise would have been left showing a stale 'request-changes' from before CR-003 was fixed.

business_review.item: AC1: Backup is refreshed (or recreated) on each connect that modifies the file
business_review.notes: Refreshed on the not-yet-managed -> managed transition and when an already-managed file's backup is missing (rebuilt from stripped content). Once a backup exists for an already-managed file, later connects that further modify the file (e.g. allowlist/env changes) do not refresh it. This literal partial against AC1's wording (CR-002) was explicitly accepted by the user as intentional — it mirrors the already-accepted codex-desktop precedent, and AC3's no-restore redesign means a backup's freshness no longer affects correctness, only the usefulness of its advisory manual-recovery snapshot.

business_review.item: AC2: After a successful disconnect the backup file is removed
business_review.notes: removeClaudeCodeOtlpConfig now unconditionally unlinks an existing backup after any successful full removal, not just the previously-empty-only case.

business_review.item: AC3: Disconnect never restores values changed/removed by the user after connect
business_review.notes: The isEmpty branch's raw backup-restore-and-write was removed entirely; disconnect only ever writes the live-derived `stripped` result or deletes the file.

business_review.item: AC4 (plan's clarification assumption): disconnect must derive the result from the current live settings file via surgical strip, deleting the file when nothing foreign remains, instead of restoring the backup
business_review.notes: Implemented via the shared stripCodemieManagedContent helper; usedBackup field and its CLI warning were removed, confirming no restore path remains.

standards_review.notes: Fix-up commit uses Conventional Commits with allowed type (fix) and allowed 'proxy' scope.
